text.en:
COMPASS Portal. The COMPASS Portal is hereby institutionalized
as the unified and publicly accessible digital platform that may utilize distributed ledger
technology, including but not limited to blockchain or other emerging technologies, for
the disclosure, consolidation, and publication of budget, expenditure, procurement, and
other transparency-related information required under existing laws, rules, regulations,
and issuances.
The Portal shall promote transparency, accountability, and public participation by
providing timely, reliable, and user-friendly access to government financial and
performance information across the budget cycle. To this end, the Portal shall, to the
extent practicable and consistent with applicable laws, adhere to principles of data
integrity, authenticity, interoperability, accessibility, traceability, auditability,
cybersecurity, and operational resilience.
The Portal shall be capable of interfacing with existing government systems,
including but not limited to the IFMIS, Budget and Treasury Management System
(BTMS), Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (PhilGEPS), Digital
2

Information for Monitoring and Evaluation (DIME), the E-Gov PH App, and such other
systems as may be identified by the DBM.
For purposes of efficiency and cost-effectiveness, the DBM may utilize, enhance,
consolidate, or repurpose existing government digital platforms and facilities in
implementing the Portal, subject to the requirements and objectives of this Order.

Covered Agencies. All concerned national government agencies
(GAs) and instrumentalities, including government owned or -controlled corporations
and government financial institutions, are hereby directed, and LGUs are hereby
encouraged, to submit, disclose, update, and publish to the COMPASS Portal
information as may be required by the DBM pursuant to this Order, subject to existing
laws, rules, and regulations. Covered agencies shall be responsible for the accuracy,
completeness, and timeliness of such information.

Covered Data. For purposes of this Order, "Covered Data" shall refer
to information on program/project performance, including financial performance and the
status of implementation and completion, as well as procurement and other
transparency-related information generated across the entire national budget cycle.
All Covered Data utilized under this Order shall remain under the lawful control,
access, and regulatory supervision of the Philippine Government, in accordance with
existing laws, rules, and regulations.

Scope and Limitations. All programs, projects, and activities
funded, administered, or implemented, including those projects funded through
public-private partnerships or foreign-assisted programs, insofar as they utilize,
disburse, or account for public funds through GAs or other relevant government
mechanisms, shall be disclosed in the COMPASS Portal.
The disclosure requirement under this Order shall not apply to information whose
publication is prohibited by law or would compromise national defense or national
security, violate RA No. 10173 or the "Data Privacy Act of 2012," or contravene other
applicable laws, rules, and regulations. Where specific portions of Covered Data are
withheld or redacted pursuant to law, the concerned agency shall publish an exception
or redaction log indicating the legal basis, approving authority, and date of such
withholding or redaction, while retaining complete records for authorized oversight and
audit purposes.
Nothing in this Order shall be construed to diminish, restrict, or otherwise limit
existing transparency and disclosure obligations under applicable laws, rules, and
regulations.

Agency Directives. To ensure effective implementation of this Order,
the DBM, DICT, Department of the Interior and Local Government (DIL.G), and
Department of Finance (DOF) shall undertake the following responsibilities, subject to
existing laws, rules, and regulations:
a. The DBM shall serve as the lead implementing agency responsible for
managing, operating, maintaining, and administering the COMPASS Portal,
3

including exercising custody over Covered Data to ensure its lawful access,
integrity, and long-term preservation, as well as prescribing disclosure
standards and ensuring integration with relevant government systems;
b. The DICT shall provide technical and digital governance support for the
COMPASS Portal, and shall prescribe standards on interoperability,
cybersecurity, data management, and information-systems architecture
across the portal and the IFMIS ecosystem;
c. The DILG shall urge LGUs to utilize the COMPASS Portal and, if applicable,
include disclosures of Covered Data as a criterion for achieving the Seal of
Good Local Governance; and
d. The DOF shall provide policy support on matters relating to public financial
management, fiscal transparency, revenue administration, and government
financial reporting.

COMPASS Council. There is hereby created a COMPASS Council
to provide policy direction and strategic oversight for the implementation of this Order
and the continuous improvement of the COMPASS Portal.
The Council shall be composed of the heads of the following agencies:
Chairperson
Co-Chairperson
The Council may invite representatives from the Congress, Judiciary,
Independent Constitutional Commissions, GAs, LGUs, civil society organizations,
academic and research institutions, the media, and other relevant stakeholders to
participate in its meetings as observers, resource speakers, or technical advisers.
The members of the COMPASS Council may designate their respective
alternates, with ranks not lower than Assistant Secretary or its equivalent, who shall be
fully authorized to decide for or on their behalf.
The Council shall meet at least once every quarter or as often as necessary to
effectively discharge its functions under this Order.

Duties and Functions. The COMPASS Council shall perform the
following duties and functions, without prejudice to other functions as may be directed
by the President, through the Executive Secretary:
a. Provide overall policy direction and strategic oversight for the implementation
of this Order;
b. Approve policies, standards, guidelines, and frameworks necessary for the
effective implementation, governance, and continuous improvement of the
4

COMPASS Portal;
c. Promote coordination among covered agencies and ensure the
harmonization of transparency, disclosure, and public financial management
initiatives across government;
d. Monitor and evaluate compliance with this Order and recommend appropriate
actions to the proper authorities in cases of non-compliance;
e. Submit periodic reports and recommendations to the President, through the
Executive Secretary, on the implementation of this Order and measures to
strengthen government transparency and accountability;
f. Formulate and approve policies, data standards, interoperability protocols,
and governance guidelines for the COMPASS Portal;
g. Ensure that all transparency mechanisms remain secure and
citizen-accessible;
h. Engage stakeholders in consultative and advisory capacities, without
expanding the formal membership of the Council;
Ensure that the platform aligns with the existing transparency and financial
systems of the DBM, Commission on Audit, DOF, and other oversight
agencies to establish a unified, interoperable, and open public financial data
J. Identify the responsible agency or office and the designated accountable
officer for the disclosure of every document type required under this Order;
k. Prescribe and enforce specific accountability and disclosure timelines,
ensuring that mandated disclosures are made within periods that harmonize
with existing statutory disclosure and reporting timelines;
1. Review and recommend the adoption of alternative or emerging technologies
to ensure the COMPASS Portal remains adaptable to emerging digital
standards, resilient against long-term risks, and capable of meeting evolving
public needs; and
m. Perform such other functions as are necessary to carry out the provisions of

Administrative Sanctions. Failure to comply with the provisions of
this Order may be a ground for administrative and disciplinary sanctions against any
erring public officer or employee as provided under existing laws, rules or regulations.

Funding. The funding requirements for the initial implementation of
this Order shall be charged against current and available appropriations of DBM, DICT,
and other concerned agencies, subject to relevant budgeting, accounting, and auditing
laws, rules, and regulations. Thereafter, the funding requirements for the continued
implementation of this Order shall be included in the budget proposal of DBM, DICT,
and other concerned agencies, subject to the usual budget preparation process.

Implementing Guidelines. Within sixty (60) days from the
effectivity of this Order, the COMPASS Council, in coordination with other concerned
agencies and representatives from civil society organizations, the academe, the media,
and relevant industry stakeholders, shall formulate and issue the guidelines necessary
for the effective implementation of this Order, which shall include but are not limited to:
(i) the proper and timely submission, validation, and updating, and use of the
COMPASS Portal; (il) the roles and responsibilities of concerned agencies; (ill) the
5

required submission formats, procedures, and schedules for release and revision of
information; and (iv) other relevant guidelines.

Separability. If any section or part of this Order is declared
unconstitutional or invalid, the other sections or provisions not otherwise affected shall
remain in full force and effect.

Repeal. All orders, rules, regulations, and issuances, or parts
thereof that are inconsistent with this Order, are hereby repealed, amended, or modified
accordingly.

Effectivity. This Order shall take effect after fifteen (15) davs
following its publication in the Official Gazette or in a newspaper of general circulation.
DONE, in the City of Manila, this
year of our Lord, Two Thousand and Twenty-Six.
